text: 1.看新闻。
en: 1. Read the news.

text: 我建议你把每一期的南方周末的第一版和经济版上的文章都看一遍，不管他们的标题你感不感兴趣，坚持至少三年。
en: I suggest you read every issue of Southern Weekly — the front page and the economics section — whether or not the headlines interest you, and keep it up for at least three years.

text: 三年后你就对各种重大社会事件和经济运行逻辑有了高于普通人的认知。
en: After three years, you will have a better-than-average understanding of major social events and how the economy works.

text: 此外，建议每年选一个社会热点，阅读各主要媒体的相关报道，遇到好的报道就复制保存起来，目前我选过的题材包括当代日本，离婚问题，各种诈骗等。
en: Also, each year pick one trending social topic, read the relevant coverage from the major media outlets, and save any good reporting you come across. Topics I have picked so far include contemporary Japan, divorce, and all kinds of scams.

text: 特别是要关注各类诈骗的新闻，了解骗子们的各种花招，不仅能让你免于上当受骗，还能深入了解别人会怎么给你编织一个茧房来骗你。
en: Pay special attention to news about scams: understanding the swindlers' tricks will not only keep you from being cheated, but also help you see how someone can weave a cocoon around you to deceive you.

text: 最好再去看一下新加坡《联合早报》，唯一不用FQ可以看的外刊。
en: It is also worth reading Singapore's Lianhe Zaobao, the only foreign newspaper you can read without bypassing the firewall.

text: 2.结构化的阅读。
en: 2. Structured reading.

text: 我是只书虫，虽然眼镜片不厚，但是从小爱看书，大学时，我跑到图书馆，一个书架一个书架的扫书看，但是我有个很多人都有的毛病，就是什么历史、社会、心理之类自己感兴趣的书就一直看，自己不感兴趣的书就很少涉猎，这其实很不好，容易让自己沉溺在一个小世界里，形成不断自我强化的偏见，所以后来我要求自己除了看自己感兴趣的书，每周还要看一个小时以前比较少看的题材，先是经济，然后哲学，然后会计。
en: I am a bookworm. My glasses are not thick, but I have loved reading since I was a child. In university, I would run to the library and sweep through the shelves one by one. But I have a flaw many people share: I kept reading only the books I was interested in — history, society, psychology and the like — and rarely touched what did not interest me. That is actually bad: it easily traps you in a small world and builds up self-reinforcing prejudice. So later I required myself, besides reading what interested me, to spend an hour each week on subjects I used to read less — first economics, then philosophy, then accounting.

text: 收获是真的觉得自己的世界变大了，看问题的角度也更多元了，比如每周听一小时黑格尔哲学以后，老婆开始听不懂我说啥了。
en: The payoff is real: I feel my world has genuinely grown bigger and my perspectives more diverse. For instance, after listening to an hour of Hegel's philosophy each week, my wife started not understanding what I was talking about.

text: 读书到底有用没用是一个大家长期争论不休的问题，现在，我觉得机构化阅读是在有用与无用之间取得平衡的一个好办法。
en: Whether reading is useful at all is a question people have argued over for a long time. Now I think institutionalised reading is a good way to strike a balance between useful and useless.

text: 近来，各路小姐姐们在推介的时候流行把喜欢阅读列进自己的优点，作为一条资深蛀书虫，私以为笼统的喜欢阅读并不能算什么大的加分项，喜欢读快餐文学、很大比例的网络小说，甚至是一般的畅销书对提升自己的帮助作用实在寥寥无几，晒一晒自己的阅读清单，如果上面有几本和自己业务有关的书，每年再来一两本经济金融类的书（学点金融常识能有效防止自己被杀猪盘当猪杀！
en: Recently, when young women promote themselves, it has become fashionable to list a love of reading among their virtues. As a veteran bookworm, I privately think that a vague love of reading is not much of a plus on its own: a love of fast-food literature, a large share of web novels, or even ordinary bestsellers does very little to improve you. Show me your reading list: if it has a few books related to your own work, plus one or two economics and finance books each year (learning some financial basics can effectively stop you from being slaughtered like a pig in a pig-butchering scam!

text: 如果有后悔药吃，薇娅肯定也想自己学点税法知识），然后再搭配点文学、社会科、历史类的经典名著，才能真正标榜自己爱看书。
en: If there were a regret pill, Wei Ya would surely want to learn some tax law herself), along with some classic works of literature, social science and history, then you can truly claim to love reading.

text: 村上春树在《挪威的森林里》借小说人物之口说，人生苦短，作者死了不到五十年的书不值得看，这话太绝对了，但是作者死了五十年以后还能让你知道名字的书确实更值得一读。
en: Haruki Murakami has a character say in Norwegian Wood that life is short, and books by authors dead less than fifty years are not worth reading. That is too absolute, but books whose authors have been dead more than fifty years and whose names you still know are indeed more worth reading.

text: 在这里，我要感谢一些微信阅读app，这个软件真是腾讯公司对中国人民的一大贡献，这个app让我们可以带着一个市级图书馆到处跑，还会根据你的兴趣为你推荐相关书籍，让你有了成为一个业余专家的可能。
en: Here I want to thank the WeRead app. This app is truly a great contribution by Tencent to the Chinese people: it lets you carry a city-level library around with you, and it recommends related books based on your interests, giving you a chance to become an amateur expert.

text: 3.把知乎每日热榜排名前三的话题下，排名前三的回答都看一遍，不管是不是你感兴趣的话题都要看，坚持三年，你会发现自己对任何话题都很有见地。
en: 3. Read the top three answers under each of the top three topics on Zhihu's daily hot list, whether or not the topic interests you. Keep it up for three years, and you will find you have real insight into any topic.

text: 4.坚持上班，坚持参加从小学到大学的同学聚会，维持必要到低度的社交生活，不要封闭在自己的世界里，多听听别人在说什么，在过什么样的生活，哪怕他们的话和狗屎一样没有营养。
en: 4. Keep going to work, keep attending class reunions from primary school through university, and maintain a necessary but low-key social life. Do not seal yourself inside your own world. Listen more to what others are saying and what kind of lives they are living, even if what they say is as devoid of substance as dog shit.

text: 让你痛苦的，往往很有用。
en: What pains you is often very useful.

text: 其实我最喜欢跟我的小学同学聚会，因为他们是家庭出身跟我最接近的一个圈子，他们的人生百态可以说是我人生的很多不同版本，他们走过的路摔过的跤对我很有借鉴意义。
en: Actually, I most enjoy reuniting with my primary school classmates, because they are the circle whose family backgrounds are closest to mine. The many shapes of their lives are, you could say, many different versions of my own life, and the paths they have walked and the falls they have taken are very instructive for me.

text: 5.驯服算法。
en: 5. Tame the algorithm.

text: 这个年代，大数据和算法无处不在，无时无刻都想把你拖进奶头乐的深渊。
en: In this day and age, big data and algorithms are everywhere, always trying to drag you into the abyss of pacifying entertainment.

text: 既然避免不了，你就得想办法跟他好好相处，甚至驯服她，把她变成自己的工具和助手。
en: Since you cannot avoid it, you have to find a way to get along with it, even tame it, and turn it into your own tool and assistant.

text: 你要再买一个手机，便宜款的就行。
en: You should buy a second phone; a cheap model will do.

text: 平时常用的手机刷视频也好，刷知乎也好，不妨想看什么就看什么，什么帅哥美女八卦都没关系，但是备用手机用来每周看一小时对自己成长有用的内容，不要污染这个备用手机的算法，这样系统会帮你找到很多你意想不到的优质内容。
en: On your everyday phone, watch whatever videos or Zhihu posts you like — handsome guys, beautiful girls, gossip, it does not matter. But use the spare phone for one hour a week of content that helps you grow, and do not pollute that spare phone's algorithm. That way the system will find you a lot of high-quality content you never expected.

text: 6.学好一门外语，有机会就出去走走，没机会就看看外文资料。
en: 6. Learn a foreign language well. If you get the chance, go out and see the world; if not, read foreign-language material.

text: b站上有CNN，BBC每天的国际新闻（国内的听不了）。
en: Bilibili has CNN and BBC international news every day (the domestic ones cannot be heard there).

text: 评论区有大佬说用微软浏览器可以直接看CNN ，美联社， 法新社， 卫报， 朝日新闻 ，雅虎。
en: Someone knowledgeable in the comments said that with the Microsoft Edge browser you can directly watch CNN, the Associated Press, Agence France-Presse, The Guardian, Asahi Shimbun and Yahoo.

text: 我有空去试试。
en: I will try it when I have time.

text: 7.选一个自己感兴趣的朝代，把微信读书上能找到的关于那个朝代的书都看一遍，从不同角度去了解一个历史事件。
en: 7. Pick a dynasty that interests you, read every book about that dynasty you can find on WeRead, and get to know a historical event from different angles.

text: 以唐朝为例，你把渤海小吏的《大唐气象》，士承东林的《大唐兴衰三百年》，王觉仁的《血腥的盛唐》，蒙曼的《精选隋唐大历史》看完，然后再看下《哈佛中国史》《剑桥中国史》的唐朝卷，最后还再去看看新旧唐书和《资治通鉴》。
en: Take the Tang dynasty as an example: read Bohai Xiaoli's The Atmosphere of the Great Tang, Shicheng Donglin's Three Hundred Years of the Tang's Rise and Fall, Wang Jueren's The Bloody Golden Age of Tang, and Meng Man's Selected Grand History of Sui and Tang. Then look at the Tang volumes of the Harvard History of China and the Cambridge History of China, and finally go and read the Old and New Books of Tang and the Zizhi Tongjian.

text: 看完这些，你就能理解为什么历史是一个任人打扮的小姑娘，就能学会怎么去怀疑和证明一个历史记录的真假了。
en: After reading all these, you will understand why history is a little girl anyone can dress up as they please, and you will learn how to doubt a historical record and prove whether it is true or false.

text: 8.多做事，家里的事，工作上的事，自己想做而还没做的事，不管大事还是小事，都要认真去做，纸上得来终觉浅，事非经过不知难，知与行是相互促进的，办好一件事，所得不输读透一本书。
en: 8. Do more things — household matters, work matters, things you want to do but have not yet done. Big or small, do them seriously. What comes from paper is always shallow; you never know how hard something is until you have been through it. Knowing and doing promote each other, and doing one thing well teaches you no less than reading a whole book through.

text: 9.看各类法律案件判决书。
en: 9. Read all kinds of legal case judgments.

text: 人在诉讼的时候互撕得最彻底，能让你看清这个世界很多被隐藏、伪装、粉饰过的人心与真相。
en: When people tear into each other in litigation, they do it most thoroughly, and it lets you see clearly much of the human nature and truth in this world that is hidden, disguised or whitewashed.

text: 10.看日本历史，特别是1990年日本泡沫经济破灭以后的历史。
en: 10. Read Japanese history, especially the history after Japan's bubble economy burst in 1990.

text: 以日为鉴，可知兴替啊，作为东亚怪物房的前两名，现代的中国和日本太像了。
en: Take Japan as a mirror, and you can understand rise and fall. As the top two in East Asia's monster house, modern China and Japan are far too alike.

text: 事实上，在清末新政和上世纪的改革开放，我们走的都是以日为师的道路，改革开放后大力发展外向型经济，承接世界产业转移，就是抄的日本六七十年代的作业。
en: In fact, in the late-Qing New Policies and in last century's reform and opening up, we followed the path of learning from Japan. After reform and opening up, vigorously developing an export-oriented economy and taking over the world's industrial transfer was simply copying Japan's homework from the 1960s and 70s.

text: 这一次，我不知道咱们能不能摸着日本这块石头成功过河，但我知道，很多在事情上你们不会是例外，比如房价的暴跌，考公爆热后又遇冷，被老龄化冲击后搞降本改革的医疗等等。
en: This time, I do not know whether we can cross the river by feeling for this Japanese stone, but I do know that in many matters you will be no exception — for example, the plunge in housing prices, the civil-service exam going from red-hot to cooling off, and healthcare pursuing cost-cutting reform after being hit by ageing.

text: 太平洋战争其实也很值得好好看看的，原因你懂的。
en: The Pacific War is actually well worth a good look too, for reasons you understand.
